** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Check the committed response header.** `recorder.Header()` returns the mutable header map. If the encoder sets the header after `WriteHeader`, this assertion can pass even though the client does not receive it. Use `recorder.Result().Header.Get("Content-Type")` to check the header snapshot sent to the client. ([pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/net/http/httptest))

**Explanation** The title "fix: send Content-Type application/json on API error responses" names the main change: EncodeError now sets Content-Type application/json on API error responses. It matches the raw summary, the changes entry, and the PR objectives. It is specific and concise.

It marks the manual QA box as not done and explains why. It includes the required AI section with tool and model. Frontend is marked as no UI change. Several template items (migrations, Apple MDM, GitOps, fleetd) are not present, but they do not apply to this change. The description is mostly complete.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#57753`] The requirement is that every JSON API error response uses `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. At the reviewed head, `EncodeError` in `server/platform/endpointer/transport_error.go` calls `w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")` before the domain encoder runs and before any `w.WriteHeader` call or body write. Every branch (401/403/404/409/400/422/499/408/generic status) therefore inherits the header. The fix covers the path the issue traces (`ServerErrorEncoder` → `EncodeError`) for decoding and endpoint errors. The summary reports `TestEncodeErrorSetsJSONContentType` covering 401, 400, and generic 500 responses. The test file was not read in this review, so the test result rests on the author's report. Manual QA was not done, which is non-coding and does not affect this verdict.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** [`#57753`] The whole-PR changes are three files: a one-line changes entry, a two-line header assignment in `EncodeError` with comment, and a regression test for the new header. The header assignment implements the linked requirement directly. The test supports it. The changes entry documents the user-visible behavior. No unrelated functional change appears in the summary. The repository diff tool could not read the changed blobs, so the file list relies on the supplied summary and the file read of the head revision, which shows the header line in place.
